title: footgun: namespaceBlueprints is named as though it always namespaces blueprint ids under the file's namespace.
detail: Only ids WITHOUT an explicit `id` field are namespaced; any blueprint carrying a bare explicit `id` (e.g. "cannon") is used verbatim and stays unnamespaced, so two files can produce the same global id and collide during registry merge.

title: footgun: validatePayload guards with `typeof this.linker.linkProject === "function"`, implying it links/loads the project to validate against.
detail: linkProject is never called anywhere in validatePayload; validation is done entirely from the passed-in currentModules map. The guard checks a capability the method does not use, so a linker missing every other method still passes.

title: footgun: The strict .cave schema accepts keys `swarm`, `world`, and `understanding` (line 36/35/39), implying these are valid cartridge config sections.
detail: mergeSemanticFragment deep-merges the whole parsed .cave object into runtime.config, but SysConfigSchema has no `swarm` or `understanding` keys; those values are silently carried as inert extra properties on config and never consumed by the runtime.

title: footgun: deepMergeObjects reads as a full recursive merge that combines base and override for the whole config tree.
detail: Arrays never merge — an override array replaces the base array entirely (line 15), so array-valued config sections (conditions/guidances/tutorials/knowledge) from a later .cave file overwrite rather than accumulate across files.

title: Array-valued config sections are overwritten, not accumulated, across semantic files
detail: When multiple .cave files each contribute array config (conditions, guidances, tutorials, knowledge), deepMergeObjects replaces the array wholesale, so all but the last file's entries are silently lost even though multi-file merge is the linker's purpose.

title: Explicit bare blueprint ids bypass namespacing and silently override across files
detail: namespaceBlueprints keeps an explicit non-namespaced id as-is, and mergeRegistry only fires a debug callback on collision before overwriting; two files defining the same explicit id produce a silent last-wins override with no error and no user-visible warning.

title: normalizeBpInput discards sibling blueprints when a top-level id and a blueprints wrapper coexist
detail: If a .bp file has both a top-level `id` and a `blueprints` map, only the entry matching `raw.id` (or the first entry) is kept and re-keyed; any other blueprints in the wrapper are dropped without error, so authored blueprints can vanish from the cartridge.

title: validatePayload never checks draftPool ids, so payloads referencing pools are flagged as broken refs
detail: existingIds is built only from blueprint headers and draftOptions; a fully-qualified reference to a valid draftPool id is not in the set and is reported as a broken reference, failing an otherwise-valid save.

title: CompilerService leaves the internal _editor block on compiled blueprints stored in the cartridge
detail: compile() returns the draft with _editor intact (it only early-returns when _editor is absent), so RuntimeCartridge.blueprints carry authoring-only _editor data that BlueprintV2 does not declare; downstream consumers see undeclared extra state and serialization has to special-case stripping it.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Real: a blueprint id collision between two loaded files is only surfaced through an optional onCollision callback wired to logger.debug; if the callback is omitted (or debug is a no-op) the earlier blueprint is overwritten with no error and no operator-visible signal.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Benign-ish: an unsupported file listed in the manifest is skipped with only a logger.warn and readFragment returns null; the file is silently excluded from the cartridge rather than failing the link, so a typo in an extension drops content without erroring.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: Real: on a schema failure only the FIRST zod issue's message is put in the thrown LinkerValidationError (issues[0]); all other validation issues for that file are discarded, so an author fixing one error at a time never sees the rest.
